TYTAN Technologies

The PACE is fast. The expectations are high. The contribution matters. Working at TYTAN is more than a job, this is a mission. We push boundaries, think big, and hold ourselves to the highest standard. Our mission and values guide everything we do, and we're looking for people who are driven by ownership, embrace challenges, and are energized by meaningful work. If you're motivated by impact and thrive in dynamic environments, you'll fit right in.

At TYTAN, we aim to set a global standard in autonomous air defense with AI-driven, cost-efficient systems that counter unmanned aerial threats at scale. We protect people. We protect critical infrastructure. We protect European sovereignty.

We are looking for an Senior Export Control Manager whose has understanding of defense product related export control and customs regulation to ensure full compliance with export control, customs, and trade regulations across our operations.

The role works closely with Logistics, Procurement, Production, and Engineering, while owning all export control and customs compliance topics within the Operations team, specifically related to the production and international movement of KWL-controlled goods.

You will act as the subject matter expert for both export control and customs, ensuring compliant classification, licensing, customs processes, and documentation across the entire operational value chain.

Your Roadmap to Make an Impact

Export Control & Trade Compliance

  • Ensure compliance with German, EU, and international export control regulations, including AWG, AWV, EU Dual-Use Regulation, and applicable international regimes.

  • Own export control topics for KWL-controlled goods, including classification, licensing, documentation, and audit readiness.

  • Classify products, components, software, and technology (e.g. KWL, ECCN, HS) in cooperation with Engineering and Product Management.

  • Determine licensing requirements, apply for and manage export licenses, and conduct embargo, sanctions, and restricted party screenings.

Customs & Import / Export Operations

  • Ensure compliance with customs regulations for imports and exports, including tariff classification (HS), customs valuation, origin determination, and preference management.

  • Coordinate customs processes with freight forwarders, customs brokers, and authorities.

  • Review and approve customs documentations and manage customs-related authorizations and procedures (e.g. simplified procedures, AEO where applicable).

Operations & Supply Chain Collaboration

  • Work closely with Logistics, Production Planning and Procurement to ensure compliant material flow.

  • Advise Operations on compliance implications for manufacturing, internal transfers, re-exports, and technology access.

  • Support onboarding of new suppliers and logistics partners and ensure export control and customs requirements are embedded into operational workflows and ERP systems.

  • Support item onboarding to ensure data quality across the product life-cycle.

Process Ownership & Governance

  • Develop, implement, and continuously improve export control and customs processes, SOPs, and work instructions within Operations.

  • Maintain complete and audit-ready documentation, records, and prepare and support internal and external audits, and authority requests.

  • Act as the main point of contact for export control and customs authorities and external advisors.

Leadership & Advisory

  • Act as a lead for export control and customs department. Train and advise employees in Operations, Supply Chain, and Logistics on export control and customs requirements.

  • Monitor regulatory changes and assess their impact on different processes and act as escalation point and decision-maker for complex compliance cases.


  • 6+ years of experience in defense product export control, customs, or trade compliance in the defense area.

  • Strong knowledge of German export control regulations (AWG, AWV, KWL) and customs law; EU Dual-Use Regulation required, understanding of US EAR/ITAR is also important .

  • Understanding of export control and customs rules for defense product is a must have.

  • Experience with KWL-controlled goods and complex international supply chains.

  • Hands-on experience with customs classification, valuation, origin, and broker coordination.

  • High level of ownership, structured working style, and attention to detail.

  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills.

  • Fluency in German and English (written and spoken).

Why TYTAN?

  • Build technology with real operational impact: Develop autonomous defense systems designed to protect lives and strengthen Europe’s security

  • Shape scalable defense capabilities: Work on solutions built for mass deployment, cost efficiency, resilience, and reliable production at scale

  • Contribute to networked air defense: Help integrate our systems into multi-layered defense architectures alongside sensors, command systems, and effectors

  • Develop for real-world operations: Build capabilities together with end users and improve them continuously based on direct operational feedback

  • Move fast and take ownership: Work in a focused, high-performance team where decisions are made quickly and individual contributions have immediate impact

  • Define a new generation of defense technology: Join early and help shape the products, engineering standards, culture, and direction of a fast-growing deep-tech company

  • Work with an international mission-driven team: Collaborate with experienced specialists united by the goal of creating sovereign and effective security capabilities for Europe

Our Benefits

  • Virtual stock options: Participate in our success through virtual stock options (VSOPs) at the company's current valuation

  • Monthly allowances: €106/month in flexible benefits including lunch discounts and EGYM Wellpass or shopping credit

  • Regular health care events: Health check-ups, skin screenings, mental health workshops, and an annual vitamin infusion on us

  • Referral bonus: Earn a reward when someone you refer joins the team

  • Regular team events: On- and off-site activities to connect and celebrate together

  • Corporate discounts: Exclusive employee discounts across a wide range of partner brands

  • Flexibility: Flexible working hours and hybrid work model, plus a modern Munich office built for focus and collaboration

About us

At TYTAN, it is more than just a job; it is about embracing autonomy, personal growth, and purpose. Make a lasting impact in the new era of defense! Join us to create a safer world for all.

We help consumers save time and money while making smart shopping decisions, and we support retailers and brands in engaging customers from online research to in-store purchases.

In 2024, Shopfully joined forces with the North American company , creating a global leader in the sector. Together, we reach 400 million households and serve over 1,000 top retailers and brands across 27 markets, including Europe, Canada, the USA, Latin America, and Australia.

Ready to spark your growth with us?

WHO WE LOOK FOR 🦄

Flipp + Shopfully’s Product team focuses on driving adoption and revenue of our products by identifying the biggest market opportunities, building the case for investing in them, and shipping solutions with engineering, all while representing the voice of our merchant customers.

About the role

The Senior Product Manager is a senior, commercially minded product leader who already understands digital advertising. This role requires a strong strategic thinker with good business sense and solid hands-on product skills who leads opportunity identification, builds decision-ready business cases, and works with engineering to ship.

You will work closely with Sales, Engineering, Data, and Marketing teams across markets to align on key business objectives. By combining market insight, customer feedback, and industry trends, you will make sure our products resonate with merchants and drive growth. We’re looking for someone who can ramp up quickly and contribute independently.

WHAT YOU WILL DO 🏄

Market Understanding and Opportunity Identification

  • Work with Product Marketing, Sales Engineering and customer-facing teams to understand customer needs and prioritize the opportunities that matter most.
  • Find the highest-leverage areas to invest in, and weigh customer demand against our resources, capabilities and strategic direction.
  • Turn complex questions into clear priorities. For example: how do we create more value for retail partners as their strategies move toward e-commerce? How do we find and build opportunities at scale as products launch in new markets?

Business Cases and Strategy

  • Build business cases that size opportunities, weigh revenue trade-offs, and structure a clear recommendation so leadership can make a decision.
  • Own your recommendations, and be ready to explain them and adapt them as you learn.
  • Lead the strategy for how our products differentiate from competitors in the market.
  • Partner with Sales and Finance on pricing and monetization so our offering stays cohesive.

Product Discovery and Delivery

  • Lead discovery with merchants, advertisers, and internal teams to define problems worth solving.
  • Prioritise ruthlessly, balancing revenue impact, effort, and strategic fit.
  • Work hands-on with engineering to define requirements and ship, from alpha and testing through broad launch.
  • Partner with Sales and Marketing on launch timing and readiness, and run retrospectives on past launches to improve future ones.

Alignment and Stakeholder Management

  • Generate cross-functional alignment (Engineering, Data, Sales, Marketing, Content) with a shared focus on goals and timing.
  • Work across markets and levels of seniority, including senior leadership, with confidence.
  • Track progress and impact of product initiatives and communicate results clearly.
  • Build relationships with industry analysts, partners, and customers, and represent Flipp + Shopfully at conferences and industry events where relevant.

WHAT YOU WILL NEED🪄

Must-haves

  • Digital advertising foundations: supply vs. demand, how exchanges, SSPs, and DSPs work, programmatic bidding, pricing models (CPM, CPC, CPV), and fill rate and yield. Ideally gained in ad tech, a retail media network, a publisher, or a marketplace.
  • Proven experience building business cases: sizing opportunities, weighing revenue trade-offs, and structuring recommendations for decisions.
  • High autonomy: you figure things out, own the outcome and don’t need close management.
  • Genuine excitement about using AI tools and rethinking how work gets done.
  • Hands-on product skills: discovery, prioritisation, and working with engineering to ship, not only strategy.
  • Stakeholder management, with the confidence to work across markets and levels of seniority.
  • A scrappy, curious and confident approach. You’re hungry to make an impact.

👉 At our company, we value diversity and actively encourage it — we believe a variety of perspectives and backgrounds makes us stronger. We focus on potential rather than on having a “perfect” CV. If this role excites you and you believe you could grow into it — even if you don’t tick every single box in the requirements — we’d love to hear from you!

NICE TO HAVE 🎆

  • Retail, CPG, or retail media background
  • Multi-market experience
  • Can speak Italian or German

LOCATION 🌐

While we have offices in Milan, Berlin, Barcelona, you can benefit from our flexible hybrid model (full remote available), empowering you to work where you're most effective.

HOURS ⏰
Your manager and several partner teams are in North America, so you’ll need to be flexible about working some later hours, beyond a standard 9-5 CET.

WHAT YOU WILL FIND AT SHOPFULLY 🤗

🌎 An opportunity to thrive in a rapidly scaling multinational company

🕶️ A vibrant, informal, and inclusive work environment

🧠 We champion autonomy, flexibility, and a hybrid work model, empowering you to own your work

📚 Access to learning opportunities and regular feedback sessions

🍓 Enjoy our central, modern offices featuring fresh snacks, coffee (including vegan options!), and ergonomic setups

🎉 Engage in meaningful team events: offsites, happy hours, company parties and celebrations that unite us beyond daily tasks

💻We provide all the necessary equipment for you to work effectively and set up your workspace, wherever you are

🧰 Benefit from additional country-specific advantages based on local contracts and practices

WHO WE ARE 💜

We’re a team of 450 people (and counting!), from 30 different nationalities. We’re on a mission to innovate, and we believe the key to that is seeing the world through a variety of perspectives. That’s why building a more diverse team, as well as bringing in even more talent, is so important for us.

TO FEEL AT HOME 🛋️ IN SHOPFULLY YOU NEED 🎯

  • Progress Over Perfection: We move forward. Always. In a fast-moving world, speed with purpose beats certainty without action. Momentum matters—not for its own sake, but because it drives results.
  • Clarity Through Transparency: We bring each other along. We work in teams, not silos. Transparency gives context, and context enables action. That means we share decisions early, publish work in progress, and document outcomes so others can learn, move faster, and build better.
  • Learn Loudly: We grow by doing and by daring. Big bets unlock big breakthroughs. But real innovation demands risk, and risk always carries the possibility of failure. That’s not a flaw. It’s the price of ambition.
  • Challenge with Empathy: We speak up, even when it’s hard—because candor shows care, and leads to better outcomes. Listening deeply is how we grow. Disagreeing openly is how we build trust.

Always Build Better: We are builders—of products, systems, and ideas. But more than that, we are builders of better. Better has no finish line. It’s a mindset.

data.description:
Hello!

I’m Allie, Head of Support at Ashby. I’m excited to share that we’re hiring a Product Support Engineer in EMEA 🎉

We’re expanding our global Support team to provide 24/7 coverage across time zones. You’ll join a global team while establishing the technical Support Engineering presence in EMEA, with the ownership and visibility that come from being one of the first Support Engineers across European time zones. We staff across regions rather than relying on on-call rotations; we’ll discuss the specific schedule for this opening during the process.

Not sure which Support role is right for you?

We’re hiring for both Product Support Specialist and Product Support Engineer roles.

  • Support Specialist owns cases and customer communication end-to-end. Troubleshoots complex issues by navigating internal tooling — audit logs, user experience testing, and API testing — to help customers reach successful outcomes.

  • Support Engineering serves as the escalation point between Support Specialists and Product Engineering. Owns integrations, supports data mapping and data migrations for customers, and resolves escalated tickets that don't require product code changes.

Please choose the role that best reflects your experience and interests rather than applying to both. If another Support role seems like a closer match, we’ll consider that in our review.

About the role

Support Engineering is the technical layer between frontline Support and Engineering. You’ll take on complex issues involving integrations, APIs, permissions, data, reporting, migrations, and workflows—using application behavior, logs, databases, and customer context to determine whether an issue can be resolved through Support or represents a product defect.

You’ll investigate issues end to end using tools such as Plain, GitHub, Datadog, databases, and the codebase. You won’t write the fix; you’ll give Engineering a well-validated escalation with reproduction steps, relevant evidence, customer impact, and a root-cause hypothesis when possible. You’ll also identify recurring issues, improve documentation and enablement, and partner with Product and Engineering on improvements. As an early Support Engineer in EMEA, you’ll establish regional operating practices and handoff norms across European time zones while bringing EMEA customer patterns to a global team.

What you’ll own

  • Own complex technical issues from intake through resolution or escalation—investigating APIs, integrations, logs, data, configuration, and workflows to determine whether Support can resolve them or Engineering should be involved.

  • Set a high bar for complex technical investigations and ensure Engineering receives clear, actionable, well-validated product issues.

  • Build trusted working relationships with frontline Support, Engineering, Product, Customer Success, and customers.

  • Identify recurring problems and turn them into documentation, enablement, tooling, process improvements, or product feedback.

  • Partner with Product and Engineering on recurring product improvements by synthesizing customer patterns, validating defects, and sharing the technical context needed to choose between a product change, documentation, tooling, or process improvement.

  • Establish EMEA coverage, handoff, and operating practices across European time zones while bringing regional customer patterns to the global Support Engineering team.

  • Track and improve the outcomes that matter: resolution speed, escalation quality, fewer avoidable Engineering escalations, frontline self-sufficiency, reduced customer effort, and customer confidence.

You should apply if:

  • You’ve worked in a hands-on, customer-centric technical role where you independently investigate ambiguous issues involving APIs, integrations, logs, data, and application behavior.

  • You’re comfortable moving between customer conversations, APIs, logs, databases, product behavior, and code-level context to find root causes.

  • You can distinguish a configuration, data, documentation, or enablement issue from a true product defect—and explain your reasoning clearly.

  • You write precise investigations that others can quickly understand and act on, and communicate thoughtfully with technical and non-technical audiences across time zones.

  • You naturally look beyond the immediate ticket and improve the systems around it through documentation, enablement, tooling, or process design.

  • You want to be an early technical owner for EMEA and are energized by building regional structure within a global team.

You should not apply if:

  • You’re looking primarily for a high-volume support role centered on predefined troubleshooting steps, rather than open-ended technical investigation and ownership.

  • Most of your experience is in internal IT, help desk, endpoint, hardware, network, infrastructure, cloud operations, systems administration, infrastructure maintenance, or service deployment—and you haven’t worked extensively with customer-centric SaaS applications, APIs, logs, or data-backed troubleshooting.

  • You prefer to pass difficult issues to another team rather than reproduce, investigate, and explain them yourself.

  • You’re looking for a role focused mainly on writing production code; this role diagnoses and escalates bugs but does not own code changes.

  • You prefer clear-cut problems and predefined answers over working through ambiguity with careful documentation, focused questions, and evidence-based decisions.

  • You want a narrowly defined role without regional operating ownership or projects that improve how the broader Support team works.

About Ashby

Ashby builds a suite of products that helps talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers run their hiring process significantly better. We raised a $50M Series D in July 2025 and support nearly 5,000 customers, including Shopify, Snowflake, OpenAI, Deliveroo, and Confluent. We’re growing much faster than 100% year over year, with a team of roughly 300 people across 22+ countries. Learn more at ashbyhq.com.

About Go To Market

We view our Support team as an extension of the product itself, one that ensures an optimal customer experience for customers ranging across all market segments. Here are a few points that should give you an idea of what it is like to work with us:

  • We spend a lot of time building best-in-class products since we believe a highly differentiated product is easier to sell.

  • We also spend a lot of time building a best-in-class customer experience. We aim to offer deep expertise whenever we interact with prospects and customers.

  • We strongly believe that small teams with very talented people and the right work environment deliver much better performance than teams with large headcount.

We value a strong sense of ownership, principled thinking over experience, and thoughtful communication (we put a lot of effort into using the right communication channels) - we’ll get into these and other values during the hiring process. You can take a look at our Leadership Principles to get a sense of what we value in People Leaders at Ashby.

Interview process

Our interview process is thorough and designed to give you enough information to assess whether Ashby is the right fit for you, while helping us evaluate technical reasoning, communication precision, and ownership.

  • Intro call with Recruiting — 30 min

  • Take-home assessment — 5 days to complete

  • Hiring Manager interview — 45–60 min

  • Virtual onsite — 120 min

    • Meet the team — 30 min

    • Technical & integration skills — 45 min

    • CS and Support leadership — 30 min

    • Closing questions — 15 min

Onboarding

Your onboarding will combine Ashby-wide product and company training with a Support Engineering-specific ramp plan. You’ll learn the product and support workflow, get familiar with the tools and systems used for technical investigations, and build relationships across Support, Product, and Engineering. With support from your manager and onboarding buddy, you’ll take on increasingly complex investigations as you build context, with regular check-ins throughout your first 90 days.

Benefits

Benefits vary by country and are shared in more detail during the process. International employees receive statutory benefits and, where available, employer-paid supplemental health coverage.

  • 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

  • Unlimited PTO. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it 😅

  • A $1,200 annual learning and professional-development budget.

  • A one-time $2,000 home-office setup budget for furniture, monitors, peripherals, and ergonomic equipment, plus a company-provided laptop.

  • Opportunities to spend time with teammates through an annual company offsite, team offsites, local meetups, and virtual events.

  • Extended health benefits for you and your dependents (subject to availability with our Employer of Record)

Ashby provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. Please be advised that we may use artificial intelligence-driven tools to assist our recruitment team in screening, assessing, and selecting candidates for this position.

Compensation: £75K – £104K • Offers Equity • Multiple Ranges

TL;DR – We’re looking for an experienced, Staff Forward Deployed Engineer to help build the future of AI-powered software creation. You will be a founding member of our FDE function, working directly with our customers to translate ambitious ideas into real products. This is a hands-on software engineering role: you will design, write, and ship production code. It’s a unique opportunity to scale a new discipline from scratch and solve problems with AI that no one has solved before.

 

Why Lovable?

Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.

We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.

 

About the role

Most engineering roles place you either close to the product or close to the customer. This role gives you both.

You’ll build alongside customers at the frontier of what Lovable can do, solving technically difficult problems across our frontend, backend and AI systems. The goal isn’t simply to make individual deployments successful: it’s to identify what should become part of the Lovable platform and then build it.

As one of our first Forward Deployed Engineers, you’ll also help define the function - from its engineering standards and ways of working to how it collaborates with customers and our core product teams.

If you want to stay deeply hands-on while shaping a product, a team and a new engineering discipline, this is that role. As you’ll be working directly with customers, travel up to 50% could be required depending on needs.

 

What we’re looking for

  • 8+ years of hands-on experience building and shipping production software

  • Extensive software engineering skills across the application stack with a track record of writing maintainable, well-tested code and owning what you build in production

  • Strong architectural thinking and familiarity with distributed systems

  • Ability to prototype rapidly and turn successful experiments into production-quality solutions

  • Exceptional product intuition and ability to work directly with users

  • Comfort operating with high ambiguity, agency, and end-to-end ownership

Bonus if you’ve:

  • Worked on agentic AI systems or built with LLMs before

  • Led zero-to-one product development

  • Worked in a founding or early startup environment

 

What you’ll do

  • Work directly with customers to understand their workflows, needs, and problems

  • Turn ambiguous requirements into clear technical designs and working production systems

  • Design, code, test, deploy, and operate solutions across Lovable’s frontend and backend

  • Translate insights from real usage into foundational platform improvements

  • Own projects end-to-end—from discovery and architecture through shipping and iteration

  • Debug complex issues across application, infrastructure, and AI-system boundaries

  • Shape how Forward Deployed Engineering operates at Lovable, including its engineering standards, rituals, and playbooks

  • Contribute to core product strategy, technical decisions, and cultural foundations

 

Our Tech Stack

  • Backend: Golang & Rust

  • Frontend: React, Typescript

  • Cloud: Cloudflare, GCP, AWS, multiple LLM providers

  • Tooling: Github Actions, OTEL, Grafana, Terraform, and more

 

How we hire

  1. Fill out a short form and hop on a brief intro call with our recruiting team.

  2. Complete a quick live coding exercise.

  3. Show us how you approach problems during several technical interviews.

  4. Show us something you’ve built that makes you proud.

 

About your application

  • Please submit your application in English - it’s our company language

  • We treat all candidates equally - if you’re interested please apply through our careers portal.

TL;DR - We're seeking an exceptional Design Engineer to build the tooling that makes AI-native brand production actually work at scale. You might call yourself a design engineer, creative technologist or even a full-stack product engineer who cares about craft. Here you’ll be someone who builds real infrastructure specifically in service of brand and creative output, working alongside brand designers who owns taste and direction.

Why Lovable?

Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.

We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.

What you'll do

In one sentence: build the front-end surfaces and the AI-generation systems that let Lovable’s brand team produce at scale without losing its taste.

  • Build pipelines connecting image/video generation APIs, internal tooling, and the systems brand and marketing already use (Lovable, Design tools, CMS, the marketing site, Slack)

  • Build internal apps for the brand team - plausibly on Lovable itself, which is both a good dogfooding story and just the fastest way to do it

  • Own reliability and versioning for the AI-generation system so brand output doesn't silently drift in quality or style over time

  • Work closely with a Brand Designer who owns taste and direction - you're building the system that lets their judgment scale, not just executing tickets

  • Constantly evaluate new models, APIs, and generation tooling as the landscape moves, and rebuild pipelines when something better comes along

What we're looking for

  • Solid engineering fundamentals - you have a track record of building, shipping, and maintaining real full-stack software

  • Genuine interest in AI generation systems (image/video models, fine-tuning, prompt pipelines) as a technical problem, not just as a user; you’ve built something with these APIs, even if only for yourself

  • Experience translating scrappy explorations into production-ready systems

  • Some design sensibility is a strong plus - you don’t need to be a designer, but you can tell when output is off-brand without it being spelled out, and you enjoy working closely with people who have strong taste

  • Comfortable building for a function with no internal precedent - you'll be making calls with no playbook to lean on

  • You’ll push the boundaries of what's possible with generative pipelines the way our Design Engineers push the boundaries of the web

Nice to have

  • Experience with Lovable or similar AI-native building tools

  • Prior work on marketing sites, design systems or brand tooling

  • Portfolio or side projects that show both craft and curiosity

Our tech stack

Lovable is built with tools that both humans and AI love:

  • Frontend: React, Tailwind

  • Backend: Golang and Rust

  • Cloud: Cloudflare, GCP, AWS, many LLM and generation providers

  • DevOps & Tooling: GitHub Actions, Grafana, OTEL, infra-as-code (Terraform)

And always on the lookout for what's next, especially in image/video generation APIs and pipelines. You’ll build custom tools in chorus with Lovable, while also contributing to Lovable upstream.

How we hire

  1. Fill in a short form then jump on an intro call with a recruiter.

  2. Show us some of your work you're really proud of.

  3. Show us how you approach problems during several technical interviews.

  4. In some cases, we may opt to do paid trial work.

About your application

  • Please submit your application in English. It's our company language so you'll be speaking lots of it if you join.

  • We are prioritizing candidates who are based in London or Stockholm, or those willing to relocate.

  • We treat all candidates equally and if you're interested please apply through our careers portal.

TL;DR: Be the strategic finance partner to the Marketing Org. You will own the financial architecture behind every marketing dollar. You’ll build the models, measurement systems, and operating rhythms that ensure every investment compounds into growth. This is an ownership seat with direct executive visibility, not a reporting function.

Why Lovable?

Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.

What We’re Looking For

Growth marketing strategist: You treat marketing spend as a portfolio of investments, not a cost center. You can decompose a blended CAC, trace attribution across channels, build cohort-level payback models, and tell a CMO exactly where the next marginal dollar should go and where to cut. You have an informed opinion on how brand spend, paid acquisition, and organic loops interact, and you back it with data.

Technical and data-driven: Strong analytical skills, with expert Excel modeling skills as table stakes. Comfortable with data (SQL, HEX, BI tools, or equivalent). You use AI tools and agents to automate work and move faster. Preference for technical degrees or deep technical exposure.

Service-first partner: You bring a proactive, "can-do" attitude to every interaction and own the operationally tedious work required for clean handoffs between teams.

High-slope learner: You learn faster than anyone around you, take ownership immediately, and thrive in low-structure environments. You go from 0→1 and then 1→10.

Experience: 4+ years of relevant experience supporting Marketing leadership. Strong candidates have a foundation in investment banking, private equity, venture capital, or management consulting, combined with operational experience at a high-growth startup, AI company, or scaled technology company. You learn fast, take ownership, and operate well in environments where the playbook doesn't exist yet. Bachelor's degree required.

What You’ll Do

Drive marketing efficiency & planning: Own the financial operating plan for Marketing - budget allocation, campaign ROI analysis, and investment tradeoffs to fuel B2C growth while maintaining unit economics discipline.

Build and own channel-level unit economics: Develop and own the CAC, LTV, and payback models that drive investment decisions at the channel and cohort level. Tie spend to acquisition, retention, and revenue so that marketing leadership and finance are operating from one shared source of truth. Pressure-test assumptions continuously — what's working, what's not, and where the next dollar should go.

Connect marketing performance to company outcomes: Work across the organization to ensure marketing investment ties to measurable business results. Analyze market trends, competitive spend, and channel dynamics to inform forward-looking strategy and ensure capital is deployed where it compounds.

Support experimentation, reporting, and forecasting: Partner with Marketing to size tests, set success metrics, and forecast impact on growth and unit economics. Create clear, repeatable reporting to track performance, targets, variance, and learnings that translate into action.

Accelerate with AI: Use AI agents and automation to collapse the time between question and answer. You're expected to continuously push what's possible, replacing manual processes with scalable infrastructure that moves at Lovable's speed.

About your application

Please submit your application in English. It’s our company language, so you’ll be speaking lots of it if you join.

We treat all candidates equally - if you’re interested, please apply through our careers portal.

Do you enjoy building a support practice as much as running one? Have you managed a team through change while still being hands-on enough to jump into an executive-level escalation yourself? Do you see AI as the single biggest lever for cutting repeat-ticket volume, and have you actually shipped something that proves it? Are you looking for a values-led company that cares about its employees' growth?

The impact you will have: As Technical Customer Support Lead based out of our London office, you'll run the TCS team day to day. That means setting the AI automation roadmap and personally driving at least one automation project from idea to production, building the career framework the team is levelled against, and owning the feedback loop back into Engineering on anything that touches support. You'll be the person executives and customers turn to when something P1 or exec-visible needs managing, and the main link between TCS and Engineering on product direction.

We know Diversity and inclusion are much deeper than just hiring, but it's important for us to mention it here. We welcome and embrace individuals of all backgrounds and identities at Elliptic, and this is an ongoing priority for us. We know incredible people don't all think in the same way. We want to be challenged every day. We are committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion at Elliptic. We welcome individuals of all backgrounds and viewpoints — diverse thinking drives our innovation. We aim to create a psychologically safe environment where everyone can bring their whole self to work. We are committed to creating a diverse, inclusive, and equitable workplace, so we welcome applications from everyone, even if you do not think you meet all the requirements for our roles. We foster an environment of psychological safety, where everyone feels comfortable bringing their whole self to work.

What you will do daily:

  • Run the team day to day: queue health, SLAs, and the follow-the-sun coverage model across four hubs.

  • Own executive-level and major-incident escalations, managing customer communication while Engineering fixes the underlying issue.

  • Review product requirements for anything that touches support, and flag deployments that could affect customers before they ship.

  • Own the AI automation roadmap, career frameworks and SOPs for the team.

  • Hire and grow the team, mentor and coach team members on both technical troubleshooting and their career growth, and own the knowledge base as a durable asset rather than a side project.

  • Work with the team to turn recurring incident types into self-service using AI and other tooling, and keep an eye on whether people actually use it.

  • Advocate for customer needs at the leadership table, turning what you're seeing in escalations into specific asks for the product roadmap.

  • Step in personally on the toughest API escalations when a customer's web or mobile build needs senior technical guidance.

What you will achieve in the first 6 months:

  • Have a documented, working escalation and RACI model the team is actually using, not just a page nobody opens.

  • Run at least one executive-level incident end to end, from first contact through customer communication to resolution.

  • Ship and measure at least one AI-driven automation project that visibly cuts routine incident volume, agreed and prioritised with the team.

You will be a great fit here if you:

  • Have led a technical support or customer-facing engineering team through real growth, not just steady state.

  • Are as comfortable in an executive incident call as you are reviewing a PRD.

  • Build process because it removes friction for your team, not because process is the point.

  • Care about AI, and have a clear point of view on how advanced systems should be built responsibly.

  • Stay technically sharp yourself: seek out the hardest escalations instead of only managing from a distance.

  • Use AI coding assistants like Copilot, Cursor, or Claude critically and effectively as part of your day-to-day workflow, not just as a novelty.

  • Firmly believe diverse and empowered teams make us stronger as individuals, as a team, and as a business.

Our ideal candidate has:

  • 5+ years in technical support, technical account management, or engineering, with 2+ years directly managing people.

  • A track record of building or scaling a support function, ideally in a regulated or high-stakes environment.

  • Demonstrated ability to mentor and coach team members, not just manage their output.

  • Comfort reading PRDs and giving product feedback that engineers actually act on.

  • Experience with the same technical surface the team works in daily: APIs, Datadog/Kibana, SQL, and workflow automation tooling.

  • Experience with AI/ML or enterprise B2B SaaS, including having led or closely supported an automation project from pilot to production.

  • Enough practical fluency in prompt design, structured outputs, and LLM evaluation to sponsor the team's AI work and judge when it's ready to ship — you don't need to have built the eval harness yourself, but you should know what a credible one looks like.

  • Familiarity with observability tooling, automation frameworks, and CI/CD pipelines, enough to have an informed view on what the team should build versus buy.

  • Genuine interest in crypto and blockchain, and in the compliance landscape it operates in.

What do we do?

Paddle offers digital product companies a completely different approach to their payment infrastructure. Instead of assembling and maintaining a complex stack of payments-related apps and services, we’re a Merchant of Record for our customers. That means we take away 100% of the pain of payment fragmentation. It’s faster, safer, cheaper, and, above all, way better.

We’re backed by investors including KKR, FTV Capital, Kindred, Notion, and 83North and serve over 10,000 software sellers in 245 territories globally.

 

The Role:

The way people find information is changing. Search now includes AI-generated answers, large language model (LLM) citations, and zero-click journeys. People often get an answer without visiting a website, so how a brand is understood and cited matters as much as where its pages rank.

We’re looking for an Organic & AI Search Manager to help Paddle show up well in those answers. You’ll shape how Paddle is understood, cited, and recommended by both people and machines. Ranking pages is part of that. Being cited and recommended is the rest. You’ll work across organic strategy, AI discoverability, and content, partnering closely with our Brand, product marketing (PMM), and Growth teams so the content we create is easy to find, trust, and surface in AI-generated answers.

Reporting to the Head of Web, you’ll connect the people who create content with the changing landscape of organic and AI-powered discovery. You’ll turn insight into strategy, and strategy into decisions.

You’ll also help move the work forward. You’ll help shape new content, and you’ll steer business-as-usual (BAU) updates, refreshes, and improvements that strengthen organic visibility, AI discoverability, and performance. Where it helps, you’ll draft first versions for review, using AI to speed that up. This is a broad role for someone who can move between spotting opportunities, making recommendations, and moving the work forward.

 

What you'll do:

  • Own Paddle’s organic and AI discoverability strategy, from brand awareness to category-level consideration, so we’re visible wherever our audience looks for answers

  • Audit our presence across traditional search, AI-generated responses, and LLM citation patterns, then build and maintain a prioritized roadmap based on the gaps

  • Turn organic and AI visibility data into clear content decisions for Brand, PMM, and Growth

  • Work with Creative, Social, and PR within Brand to structure, frame, and distribute content so search engines and LLMs can find and use it

  • Work with PMM to align messaging, terminology, and the topics we want Paddle to be known for, so we’re represented consistently wherever people look

  • Steer BAU content updates and refreshes, drafting first versions for review with the help of AI, and bring SEO and AEO input to new content

  • Define and track the metrics that show real discoverability (AI citation share, share of voice in LLM outputs, and organic visibility trends), and use them to create accountability across content functions

  • Link organic and AI visibility to commercial goals, and influence pipeline through the content and topics we prioritise

 

We'd love to hear from you if you:

  • Have a strong foundation in search engine optimisation (SEO), across technical, on-page, and off-page work, and are building expertise in AI and LLM discoverability, answer engine optimisation (AEO), or generative engine optimisation (GEO)

  • Understand how LLMs surface, cite, and recommend content, and have an informed view on how brands can influence that

  • Have experience working cross-functionally with content, brand, or product marketing teams, and have shaped and influenced how they work

  • Can steer content updates and produce a first draft for review, using AI to help

  • Are comfortable turning complex organic data and trends into clear direction for non-specialist stakeholders

  • Can connect organic performance to commercial outcomes such as pipeline, and explain the link to stakeholders

  • Can balance long-term strategic thinking with moving quickly and testing your hypotheses

  • Are curious about how information discovery is changing and have strong opinions on where it’s heading

 

Everyone is welcome at Paddle

At Paddle, we’re committed to removing invisible barriers, both for our customers and within our own teams. We recognise and celebrate that every Paddler is unique and we welcome every individual perspective. As an inclusive employer we don’t care if, or where, you studied, what you look like or where you’re from. We’re more interested in your craft, curiosity, passion for learning and what you’ll add to our culture. We encourage you to apply even if you don’t match every part of the job ad, especially if you’re part of an underrepresented group.

Please let us know if there’s anything we can do to better support you through the application process and in the workplace. We will do everything we can to support any accommodations needed. We’re committed to building a diverse team where everyone feels safe to be their authentic self. Let’s grow together.


Our Values

  • Paddle Together - “None of us, is as smart as all of us”

  • Paddle Simply - “Simple can be harder than complex: you have to get your thinking clean to make it simple”

  • Paddle for others - “We can realise our wildest dreams, so long as we help enough other people to realise theirs”

 

Why you’ll love working at Paddle

We are a diverse, growing group of Paddlers across the globe who pride ourselves on our transparent, collaborative and respectful culture.

We are a ‘digital-first’ company, which means you can work remotely, from one of our stylish hubs, or even a bit of both! We offer all team members unlimited holidays and 4 months paid family leave regardless of gender. We invest in learning and will help you with your personal development via constant exposure to new challenges, an annual learning fund, and regular internal and external training.

About BJAK

The original mission of BJAK is that we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region, including spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

 

The Role

The Operations Lead – UK owns the operational backbone of BJAK's UK business. You'll make sure daily operations, internal systems, and customer-facing execution run smoothly, efficiently, and at a standard that supports scale.

This is not a P&L role, and it's not a "manage from a distance" role either. You'll partner closely with the CEO to turn business objectives into strong execution on the ground, building systems, leading teams, and stepping in directly when execution breaks.

 

What You'll Own

  • Define and execute operational strategies that support growth and align with BJAK's objectives in the UK market.

  • Run day-to-day operations across customer service, administrative operations, and internal workflows so execution stays frictionless.

  • Hire, lead, and develop a high-performing operations and admin team with a strong culture of ownership and accountability.

  • Own process improvement, finding bottlenecks, automating where possible, and implementing systems that cut cost and increase speed.

  • Lead the customer support function and step in hands-on during high-stakes or escalated cases.

  • Oversee company administration and internal operations, including office management, documentation, vendor coordination, and adherence to internal policies.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong background in operations, execution, or internal business operations in tech, fintech, or fast-scaling environments.

  • Proven experience leading operations and admin teams in high-expectation environments.

  • Hands-on mindset with the ability to solve problems directly, not just delegate them.

  • Strong organisational, execution, and problem-solving skills.

  • Comfort operating in ambiguity and bringing structure to fast-moving situations.

  • Ability to work cross-functionally and drive execution without formal authority.

This Role Is Not For

  • People who want to direct operations from a distance instead of stepping in when things break.

  • Candidates who need fully-built systems and processes handed to them.

  • Those who need fixed scope and slow timelines.

  • People who avoid escalations, messy cases, or hard conversations with vendors and staff.

  • People who produce long updates without clear decisions or next actions.

Location

  • This role is based in the United Kingdom. This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our United Kingdom office at least 3 days per week.

Language

  • English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Role-specific interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1-2 weeks from the start of the interview process.

Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

About Delinea:
Delinea is the identity security platform that continuously controls what AI agents, humans and machines can do and for how long. It extends privileged access management from the point of access to the moment of action, using just-in-time authorization to reduce standing privilege across on-premises, multi-cloud and short-lived infrastructure, without adding friction for legitimate users. Delinea provides visibility across every identity type, scores the risk each one carries, and preserves the context behind access decisions, making them auditable and defensible. It supports both static and ephemeral access, letting teams apply Zero Standing Privilege where risk demands it without replacing existing infrastructure.

Role Overview

Join Delinea as Sales Engineering Director for Northern Europe and shape how the world’s leading identity security platform is positioned and demonstrated to enterprise customers. In this role, you will build and mentor a team of 5-7 Sales Engineers across the region, develop technical strategy, and directly influence Delinea’s competitive positioning in the market. This role is based in the UK.

You will report to the EMEA VP of Sales Engineering, work directly with regional leadership, and own the technical narrative for one of Delinea’s most strategic markets. This is an opportunity to lead at scale, invest in people, and help organisations embrace Zero Standing Privilege.

Key Responsibilities

Build and mentor the SE team Lead a team of 5-7 Sales Engineers, supporting individual development, career growth, and technical skill advancement. Establish an SE onboarding program with milestones that drive demo proficiency in 90 days or less, and embed coaching and mentorship practices across the team.

Develop SE strategy and technical positioning Create a sustainable SE operating model for Northern Europe. Align technical messaging with market opportunity and competitive landscape. Identify and align KPIs with Sales Leadership so the SE function is clearly aligned to the business. Uphold demo & POC standards that include competitive trapping, Delinea value positioning, and business value alignment tailored to Northern European market requirements.

Drive customer outcomes and win rates Work directly on high-value and complex deals. Support the sales team with technical validation, architecture design, and customer proof outcomes. Directly contribute to regional revenue, pipeline creation, and technical win rate targets.

Partner across the organisation Establish a cross-functional program to regularly engage Product Management as Delinea’s “voice of the client,” ensuring Northern European requirements are communicated back to Product & Engineering leaders. Collaborate with Marketing and Customer Success to translate customer feedback into go-to-market opportunities.

What You’ll Bring (Required)

  • Demonstrated track record driving SE org scaling, team development, and customer outcomes across multiple markets; 2+ years management experience or equivalent impact from varied backgrounds

  • Strong technical foundation in enterprise security, identity management, PAM, or infrastructure security

  • Direct experience with customer POCs, demos, and solution architecture in complex enterprise sales cycles

  • Comfortable mentoring teams through ambiguity and ownership of regional outcomes

Nice-to-Have

  • Experience in privileged access management, zero trust, or identity security space

  • Familiarity with emerging security threats: non-human identities (NHI), AI agents, runtime authorization

  • Experience managing distributed SE teams across multiple time zones and cultures

  • Track record of building or improving SE organisations (ops, hiring, compensation strategy)

  • Established relationships within Northern Europe’s cybersecurity ecosystem

  • Familiarity with regulatory/compliance considerations across Northern European markets (GDPR, data residency)

  • Relevant certifications: CISSP, CEH, or equivalent (not required)

Why work at Delinea?

  • We're passionate problem-solvers helping the world's largest organizations protect what matters most: their human and machine identities.

We’re looking for a Senior Backend Engineer

You'll own the Lending API in Germany, which banks, fintechs, brokers, and comparison sites build on to offer iwoca's finance to their customers. You'll decide how it evolves and help build the features that make partners choose iwoca.

The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £5 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The team

Introducer Tech builds the systems that partners in Germany use to refer businesses to iwoca. The aim is to get new partners integrated quickly and to make applying simple for their customers. The team also looks after how partners earn commission.

Its work covers three main areas:

  • The Lending API. Developing the versioned API and the webhooks that keep partners up to date on their customers.

  • The Introducer Portal. Building the web app that German brokers log in to, to submit applications and upload documents.

  • The sign-up journey. Improving how businesses apply and how well they convert, after a partner referral.

The team is growing to have two product managers, who each focus on either the broker or the partner flow, and three engineers across the backend and frontend, including this hire.

The team currently works in sprints, with three stand-ups a week and planning every two weeks. However, there is room to adapt how it works as it grows.

The role

You'll be the senior engineer behind iwoca's broker and partner channels in Germany, from the tools partners integrate with to the internal systems that broker account managers use.

Ownership and autonomy

  • Own the Lending API in Germany end to end, deciding what to build, when to release a new version, when to retire an old one, and what iwoca can promise partners.

  • Own the developer portal and every tool partners use to integrate, from documentation that their developers and coding agents can build from to self-serve testing that needs no help from iwoca.

Impact

  • Ship the features that make partners choose iwoca, starting with pre-qualification, which shows a customer what they could borrow before they apply.

  • Make integration quick and simple, so a partner can go live with few questions and little hand-holding.

  • Automate parts of the broker funnel and the internal CRM that broker account managers use, cutting friction and the lag between a decision and the action that follows, and building agents wherever they help.

Growth trajectory

  • Set the team's technical direction and shape the product and technical roadmap alongside the product manager.

  • Align designs with the UK engineers who share the API, so German requirements shape the design from the start.

  • As well as being hands on, you’ll develop your mentoring and coaching skills. You’ll help lead the team as the most senior engineer.

You'll work with the commercial colleagues who bring in new partners, and join the team's weekly support rotation.

The requirements

Essential:

  • Backend engineering. You've designed and built production backend systems in Python – ideally with Django, though FastAPI or Flask count too. You've used PostgreSQL or another relational database in production, and kept it fast and maintainable.

  • API design. You've built and evolved APIs that other teams or companies depend on, and made the decisions on structure, versioning, and change.

  • Ownership. You've taken work from a commercial problem through to production – scoping the solution, making the trade-offs, and iterating based on how people use it.

  • Mentoring. You've helped other engineers grow through code reviews and design sessions.

  • AI leverage. You've built agentic workflows, or used AI to scale your engineering output beyond what you could deliver alone. You judge when to use it and when not to.

  • Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience.

Bonus:

  • Partner onboarding. You've helped external developers integrate with an API – through documentation, test environments, or working with them directly.

  • Full-stack. You've contributed to frontend codebases, particularly in React or TypeScript.

  • CI/CD. You've set up or maintained the pipelines that test and release a production service.

  • Measurement. You've used data, metrics, or A/B tests to check whether a change had the effect you intended.

The salary

We expect to pay from £80,000 to £100,000 for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.

We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

  • Flexible working hours.

  • Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

  • A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

  • 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

  • A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

  • Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

  • 3% pension contributions on total earnings.

  • An employee equity incentive scheme.

  • Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

  • Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

  • Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

  • A learning and development budget for everyone.

Why Harvey

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

Role Overview

Harvey's Finance Engineering team is the investment-side counterpart to our Legal Engineering team: former investment professionals who bring real deal experience to Harvey's prospects and customers. Forward Deployed Finance Engineers lead discovery, demos, pilots, trainings, onboarding, and custom builds alongside our AEs and CSMs. They translate real investment work into Harvey solutions, serving as the trust layer across the entire customer lifecycle, from the first pilot to the most complex, custom-built workflow.

Finance Engineers work on Harvey Deals, a new product built off of Harvey's acquisition of Benchmark. Harvey Deals is where investment teams run their deals — screening, underwriting, diligence, and committee materials — built in the firm's own templates and formats, with every figure traceable back to the document it came from. Harvey works with 150+ asset management firms and analyzes 178M+ documents each month; the Finance Engineering team is how that capability meets the way deal teams actually work.

Finance Engineers understand how investors think and work, and use that expertise to design, build, and refine solutions that hold up under live deal pressure. In doing so, they don't just drive adoption; they shape Harvey's product roadmap, ensuring every release is grounded in what investment teams actually need. It's a team built to make Harvey the platform investment teams can trust with their most important work.

This role is the first Finance Engineer dedicated to private credit. You will build the credit playbook — demo library, workflow templates, use cases — while running live pilots, and lead the credit practice as the team grows.

You may be asked to travel around 2–3+ times per month. Travel is always for a significant business need and typically is for 1–3 days at a time.

What You'll Do

Forward Deployed Finance Engineers on the private credit team are former credit investors who left the desk to help build the future of how credit gets underwritten. Working closely with Account Executives, they engage with direct lenders, opportunistic and specialty finance managers, BDC managers, and insurer credit arms throughout the pre-sales process and stay with them well past it — leading pilots on live opportunities, guiding lenders through what's possible with AI, and sitting down with credit teams to build screening, underwriting, and credit committee workflows in the firm's own templates and formats.

The work is the work they did on the desk: lender presentation and CIM review; QoE read-throughs and data pack analysis; cash flow and leverage modeling; sizing and structuring; covenant and credit agreement review; credit memo drafting; and comps. It continues post-close into compliance certificate review, covenant tracking, amendment and waiver analysis, and quarterly portfolio reporting, so value compounds after the first deal. Along the way, Finance Engineers bring credit-team feedback back into the product, helping shape the future of Harvey.

What You Have

  • 6+ years on the investment or underwriting team at a direct lender, private credit fund, BDC manager, or insurer private credit arm, with demonstrated ownership of live deal work: screening, underwriting, diligence workstreams, modeling, structuring, and drafting credit committee materials. Asset-based and specialty finance backgrounds are welcome. Leveraged finance, restructuring advisory, or rating-agency experience before the principal side is welcome, but principal-side deal execution is required.

  • Strong command of the documents and data that drive a credit decision — lender presentation and CIM, QoE and data pack, model, credit agreement and intercreditor, compliance certificates — and an instinct for where the numbers and the paper disagree.

Why Hawk-Eye & Why Growth Sports❓

This exciting opportunity to join our passionate and enthusiastic team will take you to elite-level sporting events all around the world. As a member of our team, you will be responsible for delivering Hawk-Eye technology across a diverse range of current sports, including Athletics, Gaelic Sports, Volleyball, Horse Racing and Motorsports. You would be coming into a Badminton Operator role as presently, Badminton makes up the large majority of our global deployments, but our landscape can shift quickly. The 'Growth' in Growth Sports is literal: we are a highly agile department built for rapid expansion, significant pivots, and the continuous pursuit of new sporting opportunities. You will play a crucial role in maintaining excellence in our current sports, while helping us deliver innovative solutions to an ever-expanding roster of new clients.

The Growth Sports department delivers our Tracking and Replay products across a wide range of sporting applications, both in the UK and globally. We are always growing and developing new cutting-edge services for our clients, and with this expansion comes the need for new faces to join our team and help drive our ongoing innovation.

Successful applicants will receive training on the basic skills and knowledge required to be a Hawk-Eye operator - and then it’s time to get to an event and get immediately hands-on with our technology! We pride ourselves on supporting the development of our people, and we look forward to challenging you in a job that is truly unique.

What Does A Typical Day Look Like?🛠

  • Pre-Match & Tournament Preparations: Liaise with key stakeholders such as broadcast personnel, match officials and other teams to ensure all contractual obligations are seamlessly delivered;

  • Technology Setup: Set up our cutting-edge Tracking and SMART Replay technologies at venues around the world;

  • System Checks: Conduct thorough pre-match system checks to ensure everything runs efficiently;

  • Match-Day Operations: Monitoring and operating Hawk-Eye technologies during matches;

  • Performance Monitoring: Keep a close eye on hardware and software, troubleshooting any issues that arise;

  • Agile Deployment & Cross-Training: Adapt quickly to operational changes, applying your technical knowledge to new sports and systems as the department expands and pivots;

  • Post-Match Reporting: Complete detailed reports to enhance future operations and client satisfaction;

  • Off-Season Maintenance & Development: Build and maintain our hardware and equipment, and aid with research and development into new projects and technologies.

Why Is This The Right Job For You? ✅

  • Passion & Innovation: Passionate about sport in general with a desire to innovate.

  • Technical Proficiency: A strong foundation in technology with a desire to problem-solve.

  • Agility & Adaptability: Highly resilient to change. You thrive in a dynamic environment where the primary focus can pivot rapidly from one sport to another as the business scales.

  • Proactive Attitude: Ability to take initiative with a willingness to learn as much as possible.

  • Time Management: Excellent time management skills to thrive in a live broadcast environment.

  • Communication: Professional and approachable, with strong listening skills under pressure.

  • Flexibility: Willingness to travel domestically and overseas and to work weekends.

At Hawk-Eye Innovations, we appreciate and value the importance of potential and growth. If you believe that you excel in certain areas and possess the passion and desire to develop further, we encourage you to apply.

What Difficulties Might I Face?🔦

Up to this point, I’m sure there have been many things that you find intriguing about the role, however, it is not without its unique challenges. Here are some that you can expect to find with the role:

Dynamic & Changing Scope: Because our department is built for growth, our primary focus can shift rapidly. You must be comfortable with the unpredictability of scaling up new sports at short notice and stepping outside your comfort zone.
